text:
Ana (product): Heads-up: planning conversation for onboarding the 'tessera-mini' family into the catalog. We need acceptance criteria, per-customer delta reporting, and an incentive plan to get customers to opt into early migration. Can we iterate here?

Diego (eng): Quick ask: do we want to require the full eval pass for GA, or allow a staged GA where basic safety + perf are required first and expanded eval later?

Rie (eng-ml): My preference is staged gating. Minimum GA gates: safety checks (toxicity / PII filters), deterministic JSON contract tests for function-call outputs, and perf targets on our typical prompt mix. Extended gate (pre-GA): full instruction-following eval and long-context stability.

Ana (product): Staged sounds sensible. Put numbers on the perf targets?

Rie (eng-ml): Proposal:
- Safety: no new regressions on safety suite (accept threshold = 0.5% false positives delta)
- JSON contract: 1000 deterministic samples pass schema and top-token stability >= 95%
- Perf: p50@64 <= 20ms, p95@512 <= 120ms on our lowest-supported GPU family
- Long-context: 8k-token tail check with <2% perplexity drift vs baseline (subset)
If these pass we call 'beta-GA'. Full GA when instruction suite within 1.0% of current catalog reference.

Nora (customer-success): On the per-customer side, customers want a concrete migration report: sample of their traffic + delta metrics (latency, cost, top-1 accuracy on QA prompts). We can build that automatically if we can instrument per-client sampling during the opt-in cohort. Is opt-in sampling allowed? Legal needs to approve for some EU customers.

Kai (pricing): For incentives: propose a 2-month credit on usage for customers who opt into the 30-day trial cohort and provide feedback via the migration checklist. Credits paid as invoice adjustment. Also propose a short-term reduced per-token rate for new installations for first 90 days.

Diego (eng): Instrumentation plan: add a sampling flag in the routing layer: `sample_migration=true` that mirrors requests to both tessera-v1 and tessera-mini and writes anonymized diffs to s3. Example path: `s3://redwood-inference/migration-samples/{customer}/{run_ts}/diffs.jsonl`. ops-bot can create the bucket and lifecycle policy.

ops-bot: Created placeholder lifecycle policy `s3://redwood-inference/migration-samples/` with 90-day retention for diffs.

Rie (eng-ml): Important: diffs must include input hash, model outputs, latency, and token counts. We'll run automated per-customer metrics pipeline that produces a PDF + CSV report for CS. Format: columns = [input_hash, prompt_len, output_len_v1, output_len_mini, top1_match, latency_v1, latency_mini, cost_delta].

Nora (customer-success): That report will be huge to hand-curate. Suggest CS dashboard with quick pass/fail flags and a 'sample 50 failing prompts' export for customers. Also ask legal about EU pseudonymization steps.

Kai (pricing): One more ask: if per-token cost drops materially (we expect ~15% delta), customers want the choice to opt into auto-billing at the new rate immediately or wait until end of their billing cycle. For billing fairness, we'll allow immediate opt-in for customers who migrate early with pro-rated billing.

Diego (eng): Rollout cohorts: internal (engineers + platform) 72h -> trusted CS partners (5 customers) 2 weeks -> invite-only wider cohort 8 weeks -> auto-roll opt-in after 90-day pin window. We'll gate wider cohort if error_rate increases >0.2% or p95 increases >15% relative to baseline.

Rie (eng-ml): QA additions: add a 'function-call determinism' CI job that runs on every model build. Also add a stochasticity probe: 10k prompts with fixed seed to measure response variation (entropy) and a tolerance threshold.

Ana (product): Pin defaults: given CS feedback, propose existing customers pinned for 120 days unless they explicitly opt in. New customers default to the latest stable model. Also provide a PIN-EXEMPT label for contracts requiring longer retention. Thoughts?

Nora (customer-success): 120 days feels more realistic for larger customers. We'll prepare a migration timeline template and offer a dedicated migration sandbox with preserved logs for 30 days post-migration.

Kai (pricing): For the incentive credits we'll need a thermally-limited budget line. Propose 10% of estimated Q launch spend as credit pool. Finance sign-off required.

Diego (eng): Operational safety: platform should verify kernel compatibility per Dedicated label before routing. If incompat, route to v1. Also add circuit-breaker: if token_error_rate > 0.5% for a customer cohort, auto-roll back that cohort.

Rie (eng-ml): For deprecation policy: announce 9 months before sunsetting tessera-v1, publish per-customer migration delta reports 6 months prior, and allow pin exceptions up to 15 months for certified enterprise customers.

Ana (product): Action items: Rie to add the JSON contract + determinism CI jobs and finalize numeric gates (due EOD Thurs). Diego to add sampling flag + s3 diff pipeline stub and the kernel preflight check (due next Tue). Nora to draft cohort invite language and migration template. Kai to draft credit proposal for finance. I'll update roadmap and set a launch-gate review meeting.

Nora (customer-success): I'll loop legal on EU pseudonymization and prepare a single-page migration checklist for customers.

Diego (eng): I'll post the initial s3 schema and a small example payload to the repo. CLI for starting mirrored-sample: `/migration mirror start --model v1 --model2 mini --customer cust-abc --sample-rate 0.02`

ops-bot: Reminder: create TRACKER ticket INV-3472 for migration credit budget approval.

Ana (product): OK. If no objections to 120-day pin default for existing customers, I'll lock that in and publish the plan. Please raise pin-exception RFCs if needed. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
